changes.finding: Value revalidation did not distinguish a missing required serialized field from a legitimate explicit zero/null.
changes.correction: Add the required-field versus accepted-legacy-form decision beside ordinary readObject invariant validation, routed to the existing implementation reference.

changes.finding: The representation warning described private-field renaming as a blanket break, without explaining successful reads that silently lose/default data under a retained UID.
changes.correction: Qualify the statement to default serialized form and distinguish stream acceptance from semantic compatibility.

changes.finding: readObjectNoData was covered, but its class-level purpose was not explicitly distinguished from individual field omission.
changes.correction: Clarify that it does not detect an individual missing field; teach readFields/GetField.defaulted as an alternative to defaultReadObject, with explicit assignment and validation.

changes.finding: A zero-valued field can satisfy the constructor value invariant even when the stream omitted a required field.
changes.correction: Add a scoped single-field ordinary-class snippet that rejects absent maxRetries while accepting explicit 0..10. Preserve approved legacy defaults as a legitimate alternative and state that referenced-object hooks may already have run.

changes.finding: Compatibility testing did not explicitly contrast omitted fields with explicitly encoded default values.
changes.correction: Add that contrast to golden-form testing under the supported-form policy.

walkthroughs.result: Current-only accepted-form policy requires rejecting the omitted-field stream while keeping explicitly stored zero. An allowed class and matching UID are insufficient evidence of presence.
Accepted legacy form requires the approved default 3, while explicit zero remains zero. Blanket rejection or a zero-as-absence heuristic would break the declared contract.

sources.version: Java SE 25 Serialization Specification, sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.4 and 3.5
sources.support: Missing ordinary fields receive Java defaults; readFields is alternate access to the same default-field protocol and cannot follow defaultReadObject; readObjectNoData applies to absent class data; referenced objects are reconstructed during field reading.
sources.verification: Primary source opened and relevant passages inspected; mechanism reproduced on Temurin 25.0.3.

sources.support: defaulted identifies an omitted serializable field; get returns the supplied default when no value was encoded. Presence and a valid default-valued payload are different observations.
sources.verification: Official API consulted; changed call compiled for Java 17 and executed on Java 25.

sources.support: Type evolution and field mapping require semantic compatibility decisions beyond stream linking/UID matching; preserved golden-form and mixed-reader guidance.
sources.verification: Primary specification consulted; no broad compatibility proof claimed.

sources.support: Filter callbacks and composition do not validate arbitrary domain field presence or content. Existing filter mitigations remain necessary and unchanged.
sources.verification: Primary API consulted; harmless denied-class hook control executed with the configured per-stream filter.

limits: Source/API target was Java 17, actual runtime Temurin 25.0.3; no Java 17 VM, other vendor runtime, installation, network sink or production deployment exercised.

The exact new readObject snippet was tested inside a single-field ordinary Serializable wrapper. Records ignore this hook, and no record, proxy, Externalizable or Jackson example was changed or newly executed.

The omitted-field producer has the same class name and UID with a valid descriptor lacking the field; it is hostile relative to the required-current-form contract, not an arbitrary executable exploit.
The denied payload only increments an in-memory counter if its hook executes. No command execution, sockets, file modification by hooks, real secrets or gadget packages were involved.

No allowed nested-object hook, concurrent file modification, compression expansion, oversized string/array, global filter factory or old production artifact was tested in this focused probe. Those existing caveats were preserved, not re-proven.
Field-presence checks do not authenticate the producer or undo nested-object effects. Compatibility acceptance is application policy, not a property inferred from hostile bytes.
Two case inputs and criteria are separated procedurally in one shared filesystem. Coordinator must isolate one case and selected skill snapshot; known development cases are not holdouts.
No actor run or measured skill-quality gain. Global registry/verify checks remain coordinator-owned.
